## Al-An'am - The Cattle

(Revealed at Mecca)

166 Verses in 20 Sections

- The Ultimate Triumph of the Truth.
- God has ordained Mercy on Himself.
- Polytheists shall themselves confess their guilt.
- Those who disbelieve the meeting of God are sure losers.
- How the former disbelievers were seized with distress and affliction - Warning against the approach of the punishment.

- The Judgment.

## Important Topics

- The Unity of the Creator of the heavens, the earth, the darkness and the light, etc - (Verses 1, 19, 73, 96)
- Everything created of clay with the fixed term of life - (Verse 2)
- Why the Book was not sent down written on paper, i.e. in a physical form - (Verse 7)
- Why the Angel as desired by the people was not sent - (Verse 8)
- All preceding prophets were also mocked and ridiculed - (Verse 10)
- God has Himself made mercy incumbent on Him - (Verses 12, 54, 147)
- The Holy Prophet Muhammad the First and the Foremost in submission to God - (Verse 14)
- None can prevent any affliction from God - (Verse 17)
- Forging of lies against God - (Verse 21)
- Those on whose hearts God casts veils - (Verse 25)
- The fate of those who deny their meeting God - (Verse 31)
- The actual worth of the life of this life - (Verse 32)
- There is no change for the Word of God - (Verses 34, 116, 115)
- Nothing has been spared from the Book (Qur'an) - (Verses 38, 59)
- Apostles sent to every nation gone before - (Verse 42)
- Satan makes evils, fair-seeming (Verse 43)
- The blind and the seeing not alike - (Verse 50)
- The reckoning of the people not on the Apostle - (Verse 52)
- Pardon for the evils committed ignorantly - (Verse 54)
- The example of how the dead will be raised - (Verse 60)
- Chastisement can come from above and from beneath the very feet of men - (Verse 65)
- To shun vain discourses on the Signs of God - (Verse 68)
- To shun the society of those who treat religion as sport and who are puffed up with the pride of their wealth and position - (Verse 70)
- True guidance comes only from God - (Verse 71)
- The day when the Trumpet will be blown (or the spirits will be blown into the bodies) - (Verse <{["Q", "6:73"]}>)
- Abraham's exhortation to his god-father, his uncle Aazar - (Verse 74)
- Abraham's arguments on the identification of the True Lord of the Universe - (Verses 76-80)
- Those who believe and mix not faith with falsehood - (Verse 82)
- The Apostles of God are guided by God Himself - their righteousness - (Verses 84-87)
- Polytheism causes all good deeds, null and void - (Verse:88)
- The recompense of the Holy Prophet (This Verse to be read with the note on it) - (Verse 90)
- All men created of one single self - (Verse 98)
- God can never be visualised by the physical eye but by the realisation of the heart - (Verse 103)
- Not to abuse those called upon besides God - (Verse 108)
- There was an enemy for every prophet - (Verse 112)
- Never to take forbidden food, save when compelled - (Verse 121)
- God alone knows where to entrust His Message - (Verse 124)
- Whomsoever God wills, He expands his breast for Islam - (Verse 125)
- All men and jinns, will be gathered together - (Verse 128)
- Jinns had prophets from among their own kind - (Verse:130)
- The polytheists killing their issues - (Verse 137)
- The meat of the animals on whom the name of God not mentioned – Forbidden - (Verse 138)
- Extravagance forbidden - (Verse:141)
- The Modern Family planning forbidden - (Verse 151)
- Dealing with orphans' property - (Verse 152)
- The ideal total submission to God - (Verse 162)
- None shall bear the burden of the other - (Verse 164)

128.1:
Refer to the commentary of Verse <{["Q", "2:30"]}>, under "Jinn".
 Jinn are also conscious beings. Angels are made of light, therefore, on account of their illuminating gracious nature only good comes out from them. Jinn are made of fire, therefore, more often than not, evil is associated with them. They can also take any physical form, including debased animals. The word mala-ik is derived from the Arabic malk, not from the Hebrew root alaka. The meaning of malk, mulk, milk and malakut is possession, which is also ownership or holding. The holding authority is malik or maalik or malak, who is also the owner or the sovereign, exclusively used by the Quran to refer to Allah. The whole universe is milk or mulk and the holder is the absolute owner, Allah. Between the absolute owner and the held mulk there are dominions over which the intermediary authorities exercise control, with Allah's consent, in relation to the dominion above them. Each of these dominions is termed as malakut and each holding authority is called malak. The pagans worship these mala-ik, under misconceived conclusion, as the independent authorities, either the sons or the daughters of the absolute authority, who can speak or advocate on their behalf to the king of kings. It is because they do not have the insight, or true guidance, to view the spiritual world, as pointed out by verses <{["Q", "53:26"]}> - <{["Q", "53:31"]}> of al Najm.

translations.1: All praise is God's, Who created the heavens and the earth and caused the darkness and the light; yet those who disbelieve set up equals with their Lord.
translations.2: He it is Who Created you of clay, then decreed the term (In Arabic Ajl. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "82:7"]}>.) (of your life); and the term determined (Lit. fixed time for resurrection or judgment.) is with Him and yet (In spite of all the changes obvious to you.) ye doubt (About the fixity of the term.) (thereof).
translations.3: And (While.) He is God in the heavens and in the earth! He knoweth your secrets and your disclosures! and He knoweth what ye earn (for yourselves by your deeds).
translations.4: There came not unto them any sign from the signs of their Lord but they turned away from it.
translations.5: They have indeed belied the truth when it came to them; therefore, very soon the tidings (News- Tidings, i.e. about the Truth.) will come (be known) to them of what they mocked at.
translations.6: See they not how many a generation before them We have destroyed, whom We had established in the earth (to the extent to) which We had not yet established you (till now), and We sent the clouds to rain abundantly upon them, and We made the rivers flow beneath (their dwellings) and yea We destroyed them for their sins and raised (The modern time excavations and the findings of the ancient cities buried - prove the truth in this statement.) up after them another generation.
translations.7: And had We sent down unto thee a book written on a paper, and they had touched it with their hands, surely those who disbelieved had said, "This is naught but obvious sorcery (A similar demand was made to Moses. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "4:153"]}>.) ."
translations.8: And they say "Why has not an angel been sent down unto him (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) ?" And had We sent down an angel the matter would certainly have been decided (About their activity or efforts. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:210"]}>.) (once for all) and then they would not have been respited.
translations.9: And had We made him an Angel, We would have certainly made him a man (Even it an angel had been sent he would have necessarily come in human form for the angelic state is far from Social Contact with men of the low mentality and it would not have removed the state of their confusion.), and We would certainly have made confused to them what they (now) make confused.
translations.10: And certainly, were mocked (many) apostles before thee but that which they mocked at encompassed the scoffers among them (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "21:41"]}>; <{["Q", "36:30"]}>.) .
translations.11: Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Travel (Encouraging the study of the terrestrial conditions - and the fate of the wicked ones - and draw lessons from it.) ye in the earth; then see ye what hath been the end of the beliers (of our apostles')."
translations.12: Say! "To whom belongeth what is in the heavens and the earth?" Say thou "To God; He hath prescribed (With the explanation of the universe being God's and there being a collective stage when all will be viewed together. It is inevitable that His treatment to all will be based only on His grace. (A.P.).) mercy on Himself; Most certainly He will gather you on the Resurrection Day, there is no doubt about it; (As for) those who have lost (ruined) their selves, they will not believe."
translations.13: And to Him belongeth whatever dwelleth in the night and the day; And He is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing.
translations.14: Say, "Shall I take a guardian besides God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? while He feedeth (Sustains.) (others) and is not (Himself) fed (Not Sustained.) Say! "I (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) am commanded to be the first who submitteth himself (to God) (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "39:12"]}>.) " and be not thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) of the polytheists (Those who associate others with God in authority.) ."
translations.15: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily I fear should I disobey my Lord, the chastisement of a great Day."
translations.16: From whomsoever it (the Chastisement) is averted on that day, indeed He (God.) had mercy ('Rahimiyat' not 'Rahmaniyat'.) on him; and this will be the manifest triumph (Salvation.) ".
translations.17: And if God toucheth thee with affliction, none can remove it but He; and if He toucheth thee with Good, then He hath power over all things.
translations.18: He is the Supreme (Lord) above (In authority with wisdom and awareness.) His servants (Creatures.) ; and He is the All-Wise and the All-Aware.
translations.19: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "What thing is the weightiest in testimony?" Say thou: "God is witness between me and you; and hath been revealed unto me this Qur'an (As the divine evidence.) that I may warn you with it, and whomsoever it reacheth (Indicates the. universality of 'the mission of the Holy Prophet compared to that of those before him.) ; Do ye really bear witness that there are other gods with God?" Say thou: "I bear not (such) witness"! Say thou: Verily, Verily He is only one God and Verily I am away from that which ye associate (with Him) (Refer to Verse. <{["Q", "6:92"]}>. O. T. Deut. 5/4.) .
translations.20: Those whom We have given the Book recognise him (Muhammad), as they recognise their (own) sons; (yet) those who have lost (Ruined.) their selves, they will not believe.
translations.21: And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God or (he who) giveth the lie to His signs; verily the unjust will not succeed (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:94"]}>; <{["Q", "6:144"]}>; <{["Q", "6:158"]}>; <{["Q", "39:32"]}>.) .
translations.22: And on the day (of Judgment) We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others (With God.) "Where are your associate-gods whom ye used to conject?"
translations.23: Then their excuse (In Arabic 'Fitna', the mischief of their disbelief will not be there.) would be nothing but that they would say: "By God, Our Lord! we were not polytheists."
translations.24: Behold (In Arabic 'Unzur' Lit. See - This indicates that the whole scene of the day was visualised before the Holy Prophet or he could himself visualise it. Otherwise to Command with something impossible to be implemented will be meaningless.) ! how they lie against their own selves, and that which they forged has passed away from them.
translations.25: And of them are those who hearken unto thee, and We have cast veils over their hearts lest they understand it, and a heaviness into their ears; and together (even) if they see every (All the signs i.e. all miracles together.) sign they will not believe in it; to the extent that when they come (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "47:16"]}>.) to thee they only dispute with thee, those who disbelieve say: "This is naught but the legends (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "68:15"]}>; <{["Q", "83:13"]}>.) of the ancients."
translations.26: They prohibit (others) from it, and (themselves) keep far away from it; they only destroy their own selves, and (yet) they perceive (it) not.
translations.27: And couldst thou see when they are made confronting (Stop at.) the (Hell) fire, then they shall say, "Would that we were sent back and we would not belie the signs of our Lord, and we would be of the believers.''"
translations.28: Nay, it has been manifested to them what they did conceal before; and if they were sent back they would certainly return to what they were forbidden and most certainly they are liars (Refers to the possibility of any improvement or expiation through transmigration because of the inherent nature, every soul will always reveal itself in whatever form it may assume.) .
translations.29: And they say: "there is nothing (beyond') this our life in this world, and we are not to be raised again (This doctrine applies to those who totally deny the life hereafter or believe that they will only be sent back to another earthly form.) ."
translations.30: And couldst thou see when they are made to stand before their Lord ('Ba'eb' i.e. resurrection is an evolutionary stage from the Terrestrial life into a heavenly and a non-physical or non-material realm in which one feels his pretence before God (A.P.).) , He will say: "Is this not the truth?" They will say: "Yes! by Our Lord!" He will say: "Taste ye then the chastisement for what ye did (Used to.) disbelieve."
translations.31: Indeed, are losers, they who disbelieved the meeting (Not seeing, but Communion in some way appropriate to his absoluteness and our finiteness.) of God, until cometh suddenly upon them the hour ('Sa'a' i.e. the Hour i.e. of the Doom.) (of Resurrection)', They will say: "O' Our grief for our neglecting it!" And they shall bear their burdens on their backs; Is it not evil indeed what they shall bear.
translations.32: And the life of this world is naught but play and vain sport; and certainly the abode of the hereafter, is the best for those who guard (themselves against evil); Do ye not then understand (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "29:64"]}>; <{["Q", "47:36"]}>; <{["Q", "57:20"]}>.) ?
translations.33: Indeed, We know, it certainly grieveth thee that which they say, but verily it is not thee (The Holy Prophet) (that) they belie, but (it is) the signs of God, the wrong doers deny.
translations.34: And most certainly were belied (Our) apostles before thee, but they were patient on their being belied and were persecuted until came to them Our help; and none can alter the words ('Words' stands here for God's will Creative or Legislative. Here refers to the decision about His Prophets. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "58:21"]}>; <{["Q", "37:171"]}>; <{["Q", "37:172"]}>.) of God; And most certainly hath come to thee the tidings about the apostles (from Us) (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:116"]}>; <{["Q", "37:171"]}>; <{["Q", "37:172"]}>; <{["Q", "38:21"]}>.) .
translations.35: And if their turning away be hard upon thee (The address though apparently is to the Holy Prophet, but it is obvious that it cannot be a man of realisation like the Holy Prophet will never feel straitened. The address in fact is to the followers of the Holy Prophet who felt straitened for the people's turning away.) , then if thou canst seek an opening (to go down) into the earth or a ladder (to ascend up) to heaven so that thou bringeth them a sign (a miracle) (it will be in vain) But if only God desireth, certainly would He have gathered them all on the (right) guidance, so be not thou of the ignorants (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "52:38"]}>.) .
translations.36: Verily, only those will accept thee, who listen (to the Word of God); and (as to) the dead, God will raise them, then unto Him will they return (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "39:17"]}>; <{["Q", "39:18"]}>.) .
translations.37: And they say: "Why is not a sign sent down unto him from his Lord?" Say! "Verily God is able to send down a sign but most (Majority Condemned.) of them know not (The Sign referred to in this Verse is the same adverted to in Verse <{["Q", "6:35"]}>.) ."
translations.38: There is not an animal that walketh upon the earth, not a bird that flieth with its two wings, but they are communities the like of you; We have not neglected ('Tafreet' Overstepping by total negligence or by misplacing it. Everything has been in its proper place in the Book of Creation of which Qur'an is the microform (A.P.). Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:57"]}>; <{["Q", "7:58"]}>.) in the Book (The Qur'an), anything, then unto their Lord shall they (all) be gathered (in the end).
translations.39: And they who belied Our signs are deaf (The preaching will not avail them.) and dumb, in utter darkness; whom God pleaseth He alloweth them to go astray; and whom He pleaseth (Refer to Verse. <{["Q", "3:1"]}>. God's pleasure is conditioned with the aptitude of every individual. (A.P.).) , He doth put them on the straight (Right.) path.
translations.40: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Think ye that if cometh to you the chastisement (Any unexpected hardship even in this life.) of God, or cometh to you the Hour (hour of hardship even in this life.) (of resurrection), will ye call (for help) other than God, (say ye it out) if ye are truthful."
translations.41: Nay, Him (God.) will ye call (At the time of distress.) upon, and He cleareth (Deliver - give an opening relief.) away which ye pray for unto Him if He pleaseth, and ye would forget (the false gods') ye set up (with Him).
translations.42: And most certainly We sent (apostles) unto peoples before thee, then We caught them in distress and adversity, in order they might humble themselves (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "4:164"]}>; <{["Q", "10:47"]}>; <{["Q", "16:36"]}>; <{["Q", "15:24"]}>; <{["Q", "13:7"]}>; <{["Q", "40:78"]}>.) .
translations.43: Yet why did they not, when our punishment came to them, humble themselves? but their hearts were hardened and the devil made fair-seeming for them, what they did act (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "26:4"]}>.) .
translations.44: And when they forgot that which they had been admonished (Reminded of.) , We opened for them the doors of all things (of enjoyments); until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We caught them suddenly, when lo! they were in utter despair.
translations.45: So, the roots (Even the last remnant removed.) of the people who were unjust (Wrong doers.) were cut (Removed from the existence.) off; and all praise is God's the Lord of the worlds.
translations.46: Say: "Think ye, that if God taketh away your hearing and your sight and sealeth on your hearts, who is the god other than God that can bring (Restore.) it (again) to you?" See thou, how We display (explaining) the signs yet they turn aside.
translations.47: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Think ye, if the chastisement (When the calamities come even the good are also enveloped along with the evil ones, but for being recompensed in the here-after the calamity is not destructive for the good ones as it is for the evil ones.) of God cometh to you suddenly or openly, will any be destroyed but the unjust (The wrong doers.) people?"
translations.48: And We send not messengers but (as) heralds with glad tidings and warners; then whoever believeth and acteth (Note that acting aright or amending one's own conduct has been essential with the faith or belief.) aright, they shall have no fear (For having the eternal bliss and security.) , nor shall they grieve.
translations.49: And (as for) those who belie our signs, chastisement shall afflict them for what they used to transgress.
translations.50: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I do not say unto you (that) with (All that was possessed by the Holy Prophet, was God's and not his.) me are the treasures (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "52:37"]}>; <{["Q", "52:38"]}>; <{["Q", "7:187"]}>.) of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say unto you that I am an angel; I follow not but what is revealed unto me;" Say, "Are the blind and the seeing (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "5:100"]}>; <{["Q", "13:16"]}>; <{["Q", "39:9"]}>; <{["Q", "47:14"]}>.) alike; Do ye not then reflect?"
translations.51: And warn thou with it (What is revealed. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:50"]}>.) , the Qur'an those who fear that they shall be gathered unto their Lord (Thinking that) there shall not be for them, besides Him, any guardian or an intercessor, happily they may guard (themselves against evil).
translations.52: And drive (Prophet addressed for the people.) not away those who call upon their Lord, in the morning and the evening, they seek His countenance (Face.) ; neither it is on thee to answer for anything on their account nor is it on them to answer for anything on thine account so that thou driveth them away and thus be of the unjust (Reference to the aristocratic view of the common man which Islam was to abolish and bring those who prided over the others to the level of the brotherhood. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "17:15"]}>; <{["Q", "35:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:7"]}>; <{["Q", "49:13"]}>; <{["Q", "99:7"]}>; <{["Q", "99:8"]}>.) .
translations.53: Thus, did We try some of them by others so that they say: "Are these they upon whom God hath conferred (Obliged with blessings.) (His) favours, from among us? Doth (This is an answer to the question) not God know best the grateful?"
translations.54: And when come unto thee, those who believe in Our signs, say: "Salamun-alaikum" (Peace be on you) your Lord hath prescribed (Took upon Himself to be merciful.) mercy on Himself, (so that) if anyone of you doth evil in ignorance, then turneth (repentant) after that and amendeth (himself), then verily He (An answer to the repentance (The Sixth Holy Imam).) is the Most-Forgiving, The Most-Merciful.
translations.55: And thus We explain the signs in details so that the way of the sinners may be manifest (By comparing it with the way of the repentants.) .
translations.56: Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I am forbidden to worship those whom ye call besides God;" Say Thou: "I follow not your inclinations for then indeed I should have gone astray and I will not be of those who are guided (aright)."
translations.57: Say thou: "Verily I have manifest proof from my Lord and you belied it; I have not with me that (chastisement) which ye hasten (Asked to be hastened.) for; the judgment belongeth (to none) but unto God; Who declareth the truth and He is the best decider."
translations.58: Say thou, "If it were with me (The Chastisement.) , what ye hasten for, certainly would have been decided the matter between me and you (But it is with God.) ; and God knoweth best the unjust."
translations.59: And with Him are the keys (of the treasures) of the unseen - knoweth it not anyone but He; and He (alone) knoweth what is in the land and the sea; and (there) falleth not (even) a leaf (of a tree) but He knoweth it, nor a grain in the darkness (in the deepest parts) of the earth, nor anything wet or dry but (it is) in a clear Book (Refers - that besides his knowledge, there is with God the record of everything Refer to Verse. on Book 'Lawh Al-Mahfooz' The Protected Tablet Qur'an as a microform representing it. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "15:21"]}>; <{["Q", "34:3"]}>; <{["Q", "36:12"]}>.) .
translations.60: And He it is who taketh you away at night (in sleep), and He knoweth what ye acquire (Do or act in the day.) in the day, then He raiseth you up therein that a pre-fixed term (of life) be fulfilled; then unto Him is your (ultimate) return, then He will declare unto you what ye were doing (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "39:42"]}>; <{["Q", "5:117"]}>.) .
translations.61: And He is the All-dominant above His subservient ones, and He sendeth over you the guard; until cometh death unto one of you, Our messengers (angels) take (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "5:117"]}>.) him away, and they are not remiss (Neglect not - neither exceed nor fall short of the limits.) .
translations.62:
Then (Both the guards and the guarded ones.) they are returned unto God, their Maula (In Arabic 'Maula' Master, or Lord, or Guardian - as exactly this same word was used for ''Ali in the place of the Holy Prophet, at 'Ghadir Khumm'. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "5:3"]}>; <{["Q", "5:67"]}>; <{["Q", "4:65"]}>; <{["Q", "33:35"]}>; <{["Q", "6:57"]}>.
 All commentators take it as 'Master', 'Authority' unanimously. It means the same as used by the Holy Prophet at 'Ghadir Khumm' - but the antagonists of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt purposefully interpret it wrongly as friend.) (Master), the (only) Real One; Beware! (Now surely), His (alone) (as the Master) is the Judgment (The Holy Prophet as God's Vicegerent or the Master on the earth holds the power of judgment. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "4:65"]}>. All as the Vicegerent of the Holy Prophet appointed by him at the Command of the Lord, holds the same power of judgment as said the Holy Prophet.
 'Aqdhakom ''Ali Ibn Abi Talib' The Best in judgment among you is ''Ali as it is asserted in Verse <{["Q", "6:57"]}>, judgment requires the full knowledge of the truth and the excellent power of discretion between the right and the wrong, none possesses it but God, and the agencies appointed by Him" (A.P.).) , and He is the Swiftest of reckoners (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "33:36"]}>; <{["Q", "6:162"]}>.) .
translations.63: Say thou: "Who delivereth you from the (dread of the) darkness (In Arabic 'Adh-Dhulumaat' i.e. Darkness, difficulties, dangers and risks.) of the land and the sea, (when) ye pray to Him (openly) humiliating yourselves, and secretly (saying)"; "If He delivereth us from this, certainly we shall he of the grateful ones."
translations.64: Say Thou: "God delivereth you from them, and from every distress, yet again ye associate (others) with Him."
translations.65: Say thou: "He hath power that He may send on you a chastisement (Refers to wars and earthquakes, floods & the pestilences like the epidemics - political quarrels - Famines - and the other similar calamities.) from above you or from under your feet or He should involve you in confusion (in) party (dissensions) and make some of you taste the fighting of others;" Behold! how repeatedly do We display (The Variety of the Signs.) the signs, that they may understand (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "29:55"]}>.) .
translations.66: And belied it thy people and it is the very truth. Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I am not a guard upon you."
translations.67: For every prophecy (Every prophecy referred to here or elsewhere in the Qur'an shall happen at its fixed time. Mankind shall know it here and hereafter. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "78:2"]}>.) is (prefixed) time, And soon shall ye know it.
translations.68: And when thou seest those cavilling (Occupying themselves arguing with false arguments maliciously.) about Our signs, get thee away from them until they enter into (some) other discourse; And if the devil causeth thee to forget (this), then sit not after recollection, with the unjust people (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "4:140"]}>; <{["Q", "6:68"]}>; <{["Q", "6:70"]}>.) .
translations.69: And nothing of the reckoning of their (People involved in malicious discourses - the pious ones not accountable for the malicious talk of the people. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:63"]}>.) (deed) shall be upon those who guard (The pious ones.) (themselves against evil), but only to remind, so that they may guard (themselves against evil).
translations.70: And leave those who have taken their religion for a play (Pastime.) and a vain sport, and (whom) the (temporal) Life of this world hath beguiled, and admonish (them) thou by it (the Qur'an) lest a soul be fettered with what it hath earned, for it, shall not be besides God any protector nor an intercessor and if it seeketh to give every compensation, it shall not be accepted from it; these are those fettered with what they did earn, for them shall be a drink of boiling water and a painful chastisement for what they used to disbelieve. (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "4:140"]}>; <{["Q", "6:68"]}>; <{["Q", "21:16"]}>.)
translations.71: Say (Ask O' Our Apostle Muhammad!); "Shall we call on (any) besides God which profiteth us not nor harmeth us, and shall we turn back on our heels (Ancestral faith and practices.) after God hath guided us, like him who is infatuated (Fascinated.) by the devils, in the earth perplexed? (though') he hath companions who call unto guidance (The right way.) saying: "Come unto us;" Say: "Verily the guidance of God, that is the (true) guidance; and we are commanded that we should submit (ourselves) unto the Lord of the worlds,"
translations.72: And that ye establish prayer, and ye fear (Guard against His displeasure.) Him; And He it is unto Whom ye shall be gathered.
translations.73: And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth with Truth; and the day He sayeth "Be," it (Comes into existence - Becomes - Takes place.) "Is." His word is the truth; His is the kingdom on the day when (Spirits) will be breathed into forms (When the final forms for the final judgement will be given. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "69:13"]}>; <{["Q", "36:51"]}>; <{["Q", "78:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:68"]}>; <{["Q", "50:20"]}>; <{["Q", "54:8"]}>.) (Trumpet); the Knower of the unseen and the evident (worlds); And He is the All-Wise and the All- Aware.
translations.74: And when said Abraham unto his father, Azar (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "21:52"]}>; <{["Q", "26:70"]}>; <{["Q", "60:4"]}>.) , "Dost thou take idols for gods? Verily I see thee and thy people in obvious error!"
translations.75: And, thus (In the same manner. Refer to note on 'Malakoot'.) did We show Abraham (the governing of) the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth and that he may be of those who are sure (Attain the State of realisation or Certainty.) .
translations.76: (Thereafter) when the night overshadowed him, saw he a star; said he; "This my Lord?" And then when it did set, said he: "Hove not the setting ones."
translations.77: Then when he saw the moon rising (in splendour), said he: "This my Lord?" And when it did set, said he: "Had not my Lord guided me, I would have certainly been of the erring people."
translations.78: Then when he saw the sun rising (in splendour), said he: "This my Lord?" This is the greatest (one), "And then when it (also) did set, said he; "O' my people! I am clear of what ye associate with God."
translations.79: Verily I have turned my face (Turning the face to God means having faith only in Him and in none else. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:144"]}>.) (myself) wholly unto Him Who originated the heavens and the earth, being upright, and I am not of the associators (The polytheists - Those who associate others with God in authority.) .
translations.80: And (when) disputed with him, his people; Said he (Abraham.) : "Do ye dispute with me about God? while indeed He hath guided me; I fear not (anything) of what ye associate with Him, save that (which) My Lord willeth; My Lord comprehendeth everything in His knowledge; Will ye not then mind (Get admonished. Reminded - made to Remember.) ?"
translations.81: And how should I fear of what ye have associated with Him, while ye fear not that ye have associated with God that for which hath not been sent down any authority (Any belief or doctrine without any authority and reasonable proof should be discarded.) ; Which then of the two parties hath greater right to security, if ye (only) know?
translations.82: Those who believe and mix not their faith with iniquity, those are they for whom is security, and they are (the ones) guided aright.
translations.83: This Our argument, We gave it to Abraham against his people; We exalt (any one) whom We please; Verily thy Lord is All Wise, All-Knowing.
translations.84: We gave unto him (Abraham) (issues like) Isaac (Son.) and Jacob (Grandson.) ; each We did guide, and Noah, We did guided before, and in his (Either of Noah or of Abraham.) progeny (Descendants.) , David and Solomon, and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron; and thus do We reward those who do good.
translations.85: And Zakariya and John and Jesus (Counting Jesus as the son or the descendant of Noah and Abraham is the best justification for Hasan and Husain being called the Sons of the Holy Prophet as the Holy Prophet him-self did call them as such (A.P.).) and Elias; everyone was of the righteous (ones) (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "10:98"]}>; <{["Q", "21:87"]}>; <{["Q", "37:130"]}>; <{["Q", "37:139"]}>; <{["Q", "6:48"]}>.) .
translations.86: And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot; and everyone We did exalt (with Our apostle-ship) over the worlds.
translations.87: And of their fathers and their descendants and their brethren (The brethren of Israel, i.e. the children of Ishmael (A.P.).) , and We did choose them (for Our apostleship), and We guided them unto the straight (right) way.
translations.88: This is God's guidance guideth He with it, whomsoever of His servants He pleaseth; and if they were to associate others (with Him (In authority.) ) certainly would be vain (Since their actions were not in vain, they were not polytheists. This passage asserts the purity of the ancestors of Ishmael - i.e. the purity of the lineage, from the dirt or the pollution of paganism or any polytheistic cult - and asserts that they had the exclusive merit of what is mentioned in the next Verse.) for them what they were doing.
translations.89: These are they whom gave We the Book and the authority and the apostleship; so if these (people) disbelieve in it, indeed have We (already) entrusted it unto a people (The Holy Ahl Al-Bayt whom God Himself purified to the maximum limit of purity possible <{["Q", "33:33"]}>.) who are not disbelievers in it.
translations.90: These (The Holy Ahl Al-Bayt whom God Himself purified to the maximum limit of purity possible <{["Q", "33:33"]}>.) are they whom God hath guideth, therefore follow their guidance; Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!)'. "I ask not any recompense (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "10:72"]}>; <{["Q", "38:86"]}>; 36:88; <{["Q", "34:47"]}>; <{["Q", "25:57"]}>; <{["Q", "42:23"]}>. All the prophets were ordered to tell their people that they did not want any reward for their apostolic services but the last one of them (The Holy Prophet Muhammad) was ordered to ask his people for the reward for his apostleship. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "10:72"]}>; <{["Q", "34:47"]}>; <{["Q", "42:23"]}>. But that reward was only in the interest of the people themselves from whom the reward was demanded, and the interest was that mentioned in the last clause of this Verse referred to here and in Verses <{["Q", "38:86"]}>; 36:87; 36:88; <{["Q", "25:57"]}>.) from you on it (the apostleship); it is naught but a reminder to the worlds."
translations.91: They esteem (Value.) not God with the estimation due to Him when they say: "Nothing did God send down unto man!" Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Who (then) did it send down the Book which Moses brought? a light and a guidance to mankind, ye make (transcribe) it into papers (whereof) ye publish (a part) and conceal ye much (of it)? and ye were taught what ye knew not, neither you nor your fathers; Say thou! "God!" then leave them sporting in their vain discourses."
translations.92: This Book, (The Qur'an) We have sent it down blessed, confirming that which hath been before it, and that thou mayest warn (the people of) the Mother City (Mecca) and those around (The world all around - with Mecca as the Centre wherein stands the Holy House 'Ka'ba exclusively dedicated to the worship of the One True God with the 'House' or Family, first created as a blessing and guidance to mankind. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "3:96"]}>; <{["Q", "2:125"]}>; <{["Q", "22:29"]}>; <{["Q", "23:29"]}>.) her; and those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they on their prayers are constantly guarding.
translations.93: And who is more (Tyrant - Wrong doer. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:21"]}>; <{["Q", "6:144"]}>; <{["Q", "6:157"]}>; <{["Q", "11:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:32"]}>.) unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God, or sayeth "It hath been revealed unto me" while nothing had been revealed unto him, and he who sayeth: "I can jet down the like of what God rath sent down;" and if thou hadst seen when the unjust shall re in the agonies of death and the angels shall spread forth their hands, saying: "Surrender (Give out.) ye your souls (Indicates that soul is an entity which is taken away at death.) ; today ye shall be recompensed with a disgracing chastisement for what ye spoke against God other than the truth and (because) ye used to behave with pride (Arrogance) against His signs."
translations.94: And indeed ye come to us (bare and) alone as We created (Clearly indicates that the human soul was creative and not evolved from any other entity as the evolutionist conject. AP) you at first (In the beginning) , and ye have left behind your backs what We bestowed on you, and We see not with you your intercessors (The false religious leaders or the false gods and the deities on whom man falsely depended - The intercessors mentioned here are not those whom God has permitted to intercede - referred to in <{["Q", "2:166"]}>; <{["Q", "2:167"]}>; <{["Q", "7:53"]}>; <{["Q", "10:3"]}>; <{["Q", "10:28"]}>; <{["Q", "10:29"]}>; <{["Q", "16:86"]}>; <{["Q", "20:109"]}>; <{["Q", "21:28"]}>; <{["Q", "25:17"]}>; <{["Q", "25:18"]}>; <{["Q", "26:92"]}>; <{["Q", "26:93"]}>; <{["Q", "26:94"]}>; <{["Q", "28:74"]}>; <{["Q", "28:75"]}>; <{["Q", "34:23"]}>; <{["Q", "35:14"]}>; <{["Q", "39:44"]}>; <{["Q", "40:47"]}>; <{["Q", "40:48"]}>; <{["Q", "74:48"]}>.But those of the fancy of the polytheists.) , those whom ye asserted that they were, in your affairs the associates (In authority.) (of God); and indeed are now severed (Cut off.) the ties between you, and hath gone away from you what ye (falsely) asserted.
translations.95: Verily God is the Splitter of (seed) grain and the (date) stone (to sprout); He bringeth out the living from the dead and He is the Bringer of the dead from the living; That is God! How then are ye turned (deluded) away (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:57"]}>. Applicable also to the bringing put righteous issues of wicked parents and wicked issues of righteous parents like the (Son of the Holy Prophet Noah).) .
translations.96: He the Cleaver of the dawn; and hath made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning (Calculation of the Solar and the Lunar years.) (time); This is the measuring of the Almighty, the All-Knowing (Lord) (This Verse and Verse <{["Q", "6:97"]}> refer to the reliability of the acquired astronomical knowledge except regarding the moon which is not certain. (A.P.).) .
translations.97: And He it is who made the stars for you that ye may be (rightly) guided (Understand.) by (observing) them in the darkness of the land and the sea. Indeed, have We made plain the signs for the people who (can) know (The travellers in the deserts and the seamen even today deter-mine their direction based upon the position of the stars. The utility of the Sun and the Moon and the Stars referred to here is not all but only the aspect of it in relation to us. ''Ali Ibn Ebrahim in his commentary takes the term 'Nujoom' i.e. Stars, as the Holy Imams i.e., the spiritual guides. It is true from the esoteric significance in the way that God has not left man in his material effort without the Guiding Stars which do not err. He has not left man in his spiritual progress without Infallible Guiding Stars - (The Apostles and the Imams) (A.P.).) .
translations.98: He it is who hath produced you from one soul, then there is (for you) a receptacle (Resting place) and a depository; we have made plain the signs for a people who understand.
translations.99: He it is who sendeth down water from heaven, then We bring forth with it buds of (all plants) from it green (foliage) from which We produced grain piled up in the ears; and of the palm-tree, of the sheaths of it, come forth clusters (of dates) within reach, and gardens of grapes and Olives and pomegranates, alike and unlike; see ye unto the fruit of it when it yields the fruit and the ripening of it; Verily in this are signs for a people who believe (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "57:25"]}>.) .
translations.100: And (yet) make they the jinn (It was usual with the ignorant ones of the pagans to associate the wonders of nature which they could not reason out, to the hidden factors of some spiritual nature, other than God (A.P.).) , the associates for God, while He created them, and they (foolishly) without knowledge assign to Him sons and daughters; Glory be to Him, and (the most) exalted is He, above what they attribute (unto Him).
translations.101: (He is the) Originator of the heavens and the earth; How could He have an issue (Refuting the assigning of sons and daughters to God as the Christians hold Jesus as the son of God and the heathens worshipping the angels as His daughters.) while He hath no consort (A receptive partner.) ; He created (Out of nothing.) all things, He is the knower of all things.
translations.102: (Behold Ye!) that is God, your Lord, there is no god but He, the Creator of all things, therefore worship Him and He over all things holds sway.
translations.103: Vision perceiveth (Even vision comprehend Him not.) Him not, and He perceiveth (all) vision (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:63"]}>; <{["Q", "22:63"]}>; <{["Q", "12:100"]}>; <{["Q", "42:19"]}>.) ; He is the Subtle (All pervading.) , the All-Aware.
translations.104: Indeed, have come unto you (clear) proofs from your Lord, whosoever therefore seest (Gets guided by them.) it, it is for his own self; and whosoever be (wilfully) blind then it is against him; I am not over you a keeper (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "20:124"]}> - <{["Q", "20:126"]}>.) .
translations.105: And thus do We display (To explain – to make clearer.) the signs and that they may say "Thou hast been taught and that We may make it clear to people who know."
translations.106: Follow (The address is to the people through the Holy Prophet.) thou what hath been revealed unto thee from thy Lord; There is no god but He, turn thee away from the polytheists.
translations.107: And had God (so) pleased, they would not have associated (others) with Him; and We have not made thee (The Holy Prophet.) a keeper over them, nor art thou (The Holy Prophet.) over them a guardian.
translations.108: And abuse ye not those whom they invoke besides God, lest they abuse God in transgression (Exceeding the limit.) without knowledge. Thus, have We made fair-seeming (The passage apparently makes God responsible for the fair- seemingness of the deeds of the infidels but actually their own short-coming itself is responsible for it. Refer to note on action and reaction in Sura al-Fatiha, "Iyyaka Na'budu" (<{["Q", "1:5"]}>).) to every people their deeds, then unto their Lord is their return, so He will inform them of what they did.
translations.109: And they swear by God with the strongest of their oaths that if came unto them a sign, they would most certainly believe in it; Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily signs are with God, but what should make ye know that when it cometh, they will not believe (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:112"]}>; <{["Q", "7:146"]}>.) ."
translations.110: And We will turn (aside) their hearts and their visions, even as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their contumacy (Inordinacy. Refer to note on action and reaction in Sura al-Fatiha, "Iyyaka Na'budu" (<{["Q", "1:5"]}>).) , wandering blindly on.
translations.111: And had We sent down unto them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them and (even if) We had gathered all things before them, (even then) they would not believe unless that God (so) pleaseth but most of them (deliberately) ignore (This is a continuation of Verse <{["Q", "6:110"]}>. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "41:29"]}>.) .
translations.112: And thus did We make for every apostle an enemy, the devils from among men and jinn, inspire some of them unto the others tinsel discourses to deceive (them); and had thy Lord pleased they would not have done it, therefore leave them and what they forge (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:50"]}> & <{["Q", "41:29"]}>.) .
translations.113: So that, may incline unto it (The devilish suggestions- wickedness.) , the hearts of those who believe not in the (life) hereafter, so that they may be well pleased with it, and that they may earn what they do earn (of the evil).
translations.114: Should other than God I (The Holy Prophet.) seek a Judge, and when He it is Who hath sent down unto you the Book (the Qur'an) (fully) explained (Made plain.) ? And those whom We have given them the Book know that it hath been sent down from thy Lord with truth, so be thou (People addressed through the Prophet.) not of those who doubt.
translations.115: And perfect (Because perfection is finalised.) is the word of thy Lord in truth and justice; There is none who can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing and the All Knowing (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:34"]}>.) .
translations.116: And if thou (O' man! (address is not to the Holy Prophet).) obey most of those in the earth, they will lead thee astray from God's way; they follow not but conjecture (This condemns the weak and the false thinking of the majority of the people. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "53:23"]}>.) , they only (falsely) guess.
translations.117: Verily, thy Lord, He knoweth best who strayeth away from His way, and knoweth best those who follow the right guidance.
translations.118: Therefore, eat ye (the meat) of that over which hath been mentioned the name of God, if ye be believers in His signs.
translations.119: And what hath happened to you that ye eat not (meat) of that over which hath been mentioned (Allah) the name of God, while He hath indeed made plain to you what He hath forbidden unto you, excepting what ye were compelled to; and many would lead people astray by their vain desires without knowledge; Verily, thy Lord knoweth best the transgressors.
translations.120: And leave ye, open and secret sins; verily those who earn sin, soon will they be recompensed with what they earned.
translations.121: And eat ye not of that on which God's name (Allah) was not mentioned, while Verily it was transgression; and verily Satans inspire (Note the term 'Wahi' is also used for the satanic inspirations to the wicked ones.) unto their friends, that they should contend with you, and if ye obey them, verily ye be polytheists (Thus who associate others with God in His absoluteness and authority, for details Refer to 'Fiqh'. Note: - Following dictates of Satan & his friends the wicked in using forbidden food is declared Polytheism 'Shirk. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:50"]}>.) .
translations.122: Is he who was dead, then We raised him to life and made for him a light by which he walketh among the people, like unto him whose similitude is that of one in utter darkness whence he cannot come forth? Thus hath been made fair seeming for the disbelievers what they did.
translations.123: Thus made (In the manner of those who are in darkness, satisfied with their own deeds.) We in every town great ones to be its guilty ones, that they may plot therein; and they plot not but against their own selves and they perceive not.
translations.124: And when cometh unto them (The criminal dignitaries. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "37:12"]}> - <{["Q", "37:15"]}>; <{["Q", "46:7"]}>.) a sign, they say: "Never will we believe until We (We also are given revelations not only you.) are given the like of what was given unto the apostles of God," God knoweth (This is a brief reply to the many questions about God's choice of a particular lineage for prophethood and His Vicegerency. (Imamat).) best where to place His apostleship: Soon shall befall those who are guilty, humiliation (This is a prophecy about the undignified end of such people.) from God and severe chastisement for what they cunningly plot.
translations.125: Whomsoever willeth God that He should guide him aright, He expandeth (A figurative expression pointed out in Verse <{["Q", "6:112"]}> regarding the receptivity in some and the repulsive nature in some. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:112"]}> as for the attribution of the difference to the will of God. Ref to note on Sura 1 regarding the divine action and the reaction. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "4:79"]}>.) his breast for Islam, and whomsoever He intendeth to leave straying, He maketh his breast straitened and narrow as though he is climbing into the very skies. Thus, doth God layeth gnominious chastisement on those who believe not (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:112"]}>.) .
translations.126: And this (The Qur'anic path, Islam.) is the path of thy Lord, a Straight (The Right one - God's dealing with the people with recipiency and those with repulsive nature. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:126"]}>. Hence with the receptivity mentioned in the previous Verse are made the objects of the revelation i.e., the recipients of the Divine Communications.) path. Indeed, have We made clear the signs for the people who take heed.
translations.127: For them shall be the abode of peace with their Lord, and He is their Guardian because of what they used to do.
translations.128: And on the day when He shall gather them all together (and say): "O' assembly of jinn! Ye increased your strength (by seducing a great number) from men;" And will say their friends among the men: "O' Our Lord! Some of us profited by others and We have reached our term which Thou didst appoint for us;" He shall say. "The (Hell) fire is your abode, be ye the dwellers therein, save what pleaseth God; "Verily thy Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "55:33"]}>.) ."
translations.129: And thus do We make some of iniquitous to befriend (Some means by this also to control or govern the others.) the others because of what they earned.
translations.130: O' assembly of jinn and men! did not come unto you apostles from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this day (of requital') of yours?" They shall say: "We bear witness against Ourselves;" And this world's life deceived them, and they shall bear witness against their (own) selves that they were disbelievers (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:129"]}> and also <{["Q", "41:25"]}>; <{["Q", "46:29"]}> - <{["Q", "46:31"]}>; <{["Q", "55:33"]}>; <{["Q", "72:1"]}> This clearly indicates the Jinns also had apostles from among their own kind.) .
translations.131: This because thy Lord destroyeth not any town un-justly whilst their occupants were negligent (This indicates that people of every town are given the warning and respite before they are punished and they only neglect the warnings and the respite graciously given to them.) .
translations.132: And for all are degrees in accordance with what they do; and thy Lord is not heedless of what they do.
translations.133: And thy Lord is Self-Sufficient, full of Mercy; If He pleaseth He may take you away and make successors after you, whomsoever He pleaseth, even as He raised you up from the posterity of other people (This needs a reflection on the gradual development and the progress of the human race on earth and the fate of the rebellious ones of the people of yore.) .
translations.134: Verily what ye are promised, will certainly come to pass, and ye cannot make (God) helpless (Prevent or defeat.) (against it).
translations.135: Say! "O' My people (Address to those who are obstinate, The proud ones of their wealth and the worldly positions) ! Act ye according to your ability; verily I too act, then soon will ye know for whom (of us) will be the abode (Whatever be the vicissitude, the ultimate is with the righteous ones. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "28:83"]}> - The abode stands for the ultimate resting which is only for the righteous.) of the (good) end (of bliss); Verily shall not succeed the unjust (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:124"]}> - <{["Q", "6:138"]}>.) ."
translations.136: They assign unto God from what He hath created of tilth and cattle, and say: "This is for God, according to their assertion, and this for our associates (Their associate false gods whom they associate with the Lord.) , then what is for their associates reacheth not unto God, and whatever be for God, it reacheth their associates; (How) evil is what they judge!"
translations.137: And thus (Connects to the previous Verse the custodian a of the temple and not the idols.) their "Associates have made fair-seeming to most of the polytheists the slaying of their (own) children that they may cause them to perish (Which leads only the destruction.) , and confound unto them their religion, and if God hath desired (If God had only willed, He would have forced them not to do it, but this life is the state of freedom of free choice and not of compulsion.) they would not have done so, therefore leave them and what they forge."
translations.138: And say they: "These cattle and tilth are a taboo (consecrated): None shall eat them save as we (God i.e. as God pleases.) please" (this is) according to their own Assertion (Fancy.) , and (there are) cattle whose backs are forbidden and cattle they mention not (Allah) God's name on them-forging (The forging refers to what they falsely assert.) a lie against Him (God.) , soon will He (God.) requite them for what they forge (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:136"]}>; <{["Q", "5:103"]}>.) .
translations.139: And they say: "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives (Females, women.) and if it be still (Born dead.) born, then all (Both males and the females.) of them, in it are partners;" soon will He recompense them for (falsely) attributing to God; Verily He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
translations.140: Indeed, are lost those who slay their children foolishly without knowledge and prohibit (Applicable to stopping conception and causing abortions under the modern family planning and otherwise.) they what God hath given them, forging falsehood against God. Indeed, they have gone astray and they are not guided aright.
translations.141: And He it is who produceth gardens (of vine) trellised and untrellised, and date palms and tilth of various (kinds of food produce) and olives and pomegranates, similar (in kind) and different (in variety), eat ye of its fruit when it fruiteth (Yields the fruits.) and give ye His (God's) share ('Zakaat' the fixed poor- rate and 'Khums' the prescribed l/5th of the net profit- Ref to 'Fiqha'.) , on the day of its reaping, and act ye not extravagantly; Verily He loveth not the extravagant (ones) (This roots out and rules out all the man-made barriers created on the economic consideration of a state preventing people to move as they need to be benefited by God's provision on the earth and the ritual prohibition in this regard and establishes the right of God i.e. the prescribed poor-rate and charity in His name and condemns overacting.) .
translations.142: And of cattle are some bearers of burden and some (low fit only) for spreading (bed-or for staying.) ; eat ye of what God provideth you with, and follow ye not the footsteps of Satan; verily he is your declared enemy (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:168"]}>; <{["Q", "16:5"]}>, <{["Q", "16:66"]}> <{["Q", "40:79"]}>.) .
translations.143: (Take) Eight in pairs-two of sheep and two of goats; Say: "Hath He forbidden the two males or the two females or what is contained in the wombs of the two females? Inform me with knowledge, if ye be truthful (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "5:103"]}>; <{["Q", "10:59"]}>; <{["Q", "16:116"]}>.) ."
translations.144: And of the two camels and of the two oxen; say, the two males hath He forbidden or the two females or that which contain the (wombs) of the two females? or were ye witnesses when God did enjoin this;" Who, then is more unjust than he who forgeth (Applicable also to all kinds of conjectures about the divine affairs and authorities and matters of religion without proper knowledge of it-It is as well a warning against the modern irreligious rebellious talks. (A.P.).) a lie against God to lead astray mankind without knowledge? Verily guideth not God a people who are unjust (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "6:12"]}>; <{["Q", "6:21"]}>; <{["Q", "6:54"]}>; <{["Q", "6:58"]}>; <{["Q", "6:94"]}>; <{["Q", "6:158"]}>; <{["Q", "39:32"]}>.) .
translations.145: Say: "I find not in what hath been revealed unto me anything forbidden to an eater to eat except it be died of itself, or blood poured forth or flesh of swine for verily that is unclean or a transgression,(a) slain invoking the name of other than Allah (God), but (even so) if one is forced (Forced not by friends or the socials in clubs but by the enemy or made helpless against the use.) (to eat it) not lusting nor (wilfully) transgressing the limits, then verily thy Lord is Oft-Forgiving, All-Merciful (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:173"]}>; <{["Q", "5:3"]}>.) ."
translations.146: And unto those who were Jews forbade We every animal having undivided hoof, and of oxen and sheep forbade We unto them the fat of both, save what is upon their backs or the entrails or what is mixed with bones; this We recompensed (Temporary prohibition for a local reason.) them for their rebellion, and verily We are truthful.
translations.147: If they belie thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) then say (though) "thy Lord is full of Mercy all-embracing but His wrath shall not be returned from the people who are guilty (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "3:92"]}>.) ."
translations.148: Those who are polytheists will say: "Had (The fallacy in the argument of the polytheists is that they have omitted the fact that there is no compulsion on the part of God with regard to the human action in this life. The divine will in this regard is always legislative and not creative. Refer to note in the margin of Verse <{["Q", "6:138"]}>.) God wished we would not have associated (aught with Him) nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden (to ourselves) anything." So did belie those before them until they tested Our wrath; Say thou: "Have ye with you any knowledge? Then produce ye that unto us, ye follow naught but conjecture and ye utter naught but guessing (Talk with no authority.) ."
translations.149: Say thou: "Then, God's (alone) is the argument decisive; Had God wished He would surely have guided you all aright."
translations.150: Say thou: "Bring ye your witnesses who bear witness that God hath forbidden this," then (even) if they bear witness, bear thou not witness with them; and follow not thou the inclinations of those who belie Our signs; and those who believe not in the hereafter, and while they with their Lord equalize (In authority.) (others).
translations.151: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Come ye! I will recite (unto) you what your Lord hath forbidden to you that ye associate not with Him anything and to ( your) parents be good, and slay (Applicable to the unwarranted and 'Family Planning'.) ye not your children for (fear of) poverty; We provide for you and for them, and draw ye not near unto shameful (Referable to the unnatural methods of preventing conception.) deeds, that which be apparent and that which be concealed, and kill ye not the soul which God hath forbidden save for justice; This He enjoineth you with, so that ye may understand."
translations.152: And approach ye not the property of an orphan save that be in the best manner till he attaineth his maturity; Give ye full measure and full weight in (perfect) justice; We task not a soul but according to his ability, and when ye speak be just; though it be against a kinsman; and fulfil ye God's covenant (This serves as a reminder as well as a warning to the Muslims particularly about the Last Covenant taken from them by God through His apostle the Holy Prophet on 18th Dhu 'l-Hijja 10 AH at 'Ghadir Khumm'.) ; This He enjoineth you with so that ye may be mindful (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "4:6"]}>, <{["Q", "17:34"]}>.) .
translations.153: And (know ye) Verily this My path, is the straight (right) one, so ye follow it, and follow ye not (other) ways for they will scatter you away from His path; this doth He enjoin you with, so that ye may guard (yourselves against evil) (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:160"]}>.) .
translations.154: Besides, We gave Moses the Book completing (our favours) on those who would do good and explaining all things in details, and a guidance and a mercy, so that in the meeting (The day of resurrection and for the Final Judgement. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "35:42"]}>.) of their Lord they may believe.
translations.155: And this (Qur'an) is a Book, We have sent it down, blessed, so follow it, and guard (your-selves against evil) so that ye may be done mercy (Receive God's mercy.) .
translations.156: Lest ye (Polytheists) should say "that the Book (from God) was sent down unto two parties (This indicates that the previous Scriptures were sectional, not universal, which fact is confirmed by several passages of the Qur'an pointing out that Moses and Jesus were sent but only to the Children of Israel-This is clearly and openly acknowledged by the Bible of the Christian church and the national character of the belief in godhead as presented in the Old and the New Testaments Math-15/22-26 10/5 - John- 16/5-14 Etc.) (the Christians and the Jews) before us, and verily we were of what they read, unaware."
translations.157: Or (lest) ye should say: "Had only been sent unto us a book we should have been better guided than they;" so indeed hath (now) come unto you a manifest proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy; who then is more unjust than he who belieth the signs of God and turneth away from them? Soon shall We recompense those who turn away from Our signs with an evil chastisement for what they used to turn away (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:5"]}>, <{["Q", "6:21"]}>, <{["Q", "6:94"]}>, <{["Q", "6:145"]}>, 39:92.) .
translations.158: They wait not but (to see) that (Refer to the adamance of the disbelievers.) come unto them the angels, or cometh thy Lord (Himself), or that come (unto them) some signs of thy Lord; on the day when come (i.e. the good deeds of the one who believed but acted only after the sign.) some of the signs of thy Lord, its faith shall profit not a soul which believed not before, or earned good through its faith; Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Wait ye! Verily We too are waiting (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "7:5"]}>.) ."
translations.159: Verily those who divided their religion and became parties, thou hast no concern with anything of them; their affair is with God only, then will He inform them of what they did (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:154"]}>.) .
translations.160: Whosoever cometh with a good (deed) for him shall be ten (According to God's grace.) like it; and whosoever cometh with an evil (deed) he shall be recompensed not but with the like (According to God's Justice.) of it, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly.
translations.161: Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Verily my Lord hath guided me unto the straight (right) path (Islam-i.e. Absolute submission to the divine will.) ; the established (Which never changes – unimpeachable.) religion, the faith of Abraham, the upright one; and he (Abraham.) was not of the polytheists."
translations.162: Say: "Verily my prayer and my sacrifice, my life and my death, (are all, only) for God, the Lord of the worlds (This is what the term Islam inspires and demands of every Muslim. That every act of his in this life secular or religious- to be exclusively for God. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:156"]}>.) ."
translations.163: No associate (In the devotion of The Holy Prophet to Him.) (is there) for Him; and this I am commanded, I am the first of the Muslims (i.e., those who submit to God) (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:14"]}>.) .
translations.164: Say: "Shall I seek other than God a Lord? While He is the Lord of all things; and no soul earneth (any evil deed) but against itself; and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another; then unto your Lord is your return, so He will inform you of what ye used to differ (about) (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:48"]}>; <{["Q", "2:123"]}>; <{["Q", "2:254"]}>; <{["Q", "17:15"]}>; <{["Q", "35:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:7"]}>; <{["Q", "53:38"]}>; <{["Q", "53:39"]}>.)"
translations.165: And He (God.) it is who hath made you (His) Vicegerent in the earth and raised some of you above others in grades, that He may try you in what He gave you; Verily thy Lord is quick in the requital (of evil) and (yet) verily He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Merciful.

exegesis.1:
God being presented here as the Maker of both the darkness and the light, is only in contrast to the dualistic faith of the Magians which give co-eternal existence to darkness as well as to light. Islam as a pure and a strict monotheistic religion establishes the truth that the ultimate genetic cause of everything in the universe, be that in the heavens or in the earth or in between them is God and none else. By its pure monotheism Islam wants to make sure for man, that the essential and the ultimate the All-Good being is the One and the Only God and none else beside Him.

Of Him comes nothing but goodness and virtue alone shall prevail and there will be no place for evil at all. Similarly, wherever God's exclusive propriety over the heavens and the earth, or God as the Maker of the night and the day, is mentioned, it is only to counter the polytheistic belief among the Jews, the Christians and other heathens. This Verse declares that all thanks, all gratitude or all indebtedness or praise, be that of any kind in any degree whatsoever, is due only to God and to none else.
exegesis.2:
'Created you', 'You' stands for Adam the Progenitor of the human species or every human being, or the address can be to any creature on earth. The origin of every earthly thing is from clay. The first term is the life until death and the second one, is the resurrection. However, all men are created from clay or dust.

Man as an individual as well as a specie, in the course of his creation passes through stages from the embryo to full grown babe, a child, a matured man, old age and death and after death the intermediary stages between death and resurrection, the Day of Judgment and its various stages until the ultimate destiny of Hell or Heaven. For each stage there is a term fixed and determined with regard to God's Knowledge of the things in the Summit state of Absoluteness. Descending from that Absoluteness, the terms become conditional, capable of increase as well as decrease. Taking all conditions into consideration in the Summit of Absoluteness, the term of a child in its mother's womb is fixed, be that short or long but the same term from the normal point of view, the term is nine months but the term for each child is subject to increase or decrease.

This is true of the term of all creatures. The fixed term is known only to the Absolute in the summit of His infinite knowledge and can never be known to any finite being unless he is particularly informed by God and the conditional term may be known to the finite ones which will not be definite but subject to change. This decrease and increase of the term is with regard to the terms of life and death and the term of various stages. The term of life here may increase, or the term of the life hereafter as said in <{["Q", "35:11"]}>. But the total term of the existence of a finite being is always fixed (A.P.).
exegesis.3: This is a repeated assertion of the Unity of God, the Only Creator, Lord, Cherisher of the Universe. He is the Knower of everything, be it hidden or manifest. Hidden and manifest are the two terms that are related only to man; for, to God nothing can be hidden for He is the maker of everything. Everything is in His view, and nothing is out of His knowledge. His knowledge envelops everything<{["F", 1]}>. This is a warning as well, meaning, let not anyone think that what one does can ever be a secret from the All-Knowing Lord.
exegesis.4: '_Aayaat'_ means signs, revelations, communications - Every Prophet or Apostle and every divinely commissioned successor of the Holy Prophet (i.e., the Imams) all were the '_Aayaat'_, i.e., the signs through whom God and godliness was manifested into this world.
exegesis.8: 'The matter would have been certainly decided' means that punishment would certainly have followed any rejection thereafter<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.9:
Even if an angel had been deputed to act as an Apostle to men, he would also have been in human form for the physical eye of man, can see things material and in some form or other - and even then, the circumstances for men would have been the same.

Abdullah Ibn Obay the notorious hypocrite had criticised, saying, that if God really wanted to send an Apostle, he could have sent one of his angels, then this Verse was revealed (F.A.).
exegesis.10: It is a reference to the people of Noah, Lot, Aad and Thamud who ridiculed the apostles, and acted rebelliously and were destroyed. It indirectly infers that the ultimate success will be of the Holy Prophet and the Jews and the Christians who ridiculed him and his message, will be subjugated under his control.
exegesis.12: This Verse refers to the ever-ready and all-encompassing mercy of the All-Merciful Lord, giving hopes of pardon for those who repent for their past evils and turn to piety and goodness amending their behaviour and giving up the evils.
exegesis.14: Some critics say that this passage and the other similar ones which present the Holy Prophet as the first Muslim<{["F", 1]}> mean that the Holy Prophet was also a convert before which he was not a Muslim. This is wrong for Islam is a term which has been used in Qur'an to mean absolute submission to the will of God and in this sense this has been used to refer to whatever there is in the heavens and the earth<{["F", 2]}>, the term Muslim is not restricted only to the human converts but includes every part and particle of the universe, in the order of which the Holy Prophet is the first one who submitted to God and the similar term of '_Abdiyat'_ has been used for whatever is in the heavens and the earth<{["F", 3]}>, and the Holy Prophet has been termed as the first worshipper or '_Abid'_, i.e., the supplicant to God<{["F", 4]}> (A.P.).
exegesis.17: Meaning the soul, the Only and the Supreme Master doing good or harming anyone, whose decision is ever irrevocable, is God and none else. Hence man needs to love or to fear only God and no other authority and to depend only on Hint and on none else.
exegesis.19:
'_Man Balagha ainnakum'_ clearly denotes that the Holy Prophet's mission was not confined or restricted to anyone particular people or place but to mankind as a whole for all times in all climes<{["F", 1]}>.

Jesus had clearly declared to his people that he was sent only for the Lost Sheep of the House of Israel and he had not told the Truth as a whole, there were yet many things to say - the Comforter to come will disclose the whole truth and will Abide for Ever:

22. And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.

23. But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, send her away; for she crieth after us.

24. But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the Lost Sheep of the House of Israel. Math. 15/22-24.

5. These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

6. But go rather to the Lost Sheep of the House of Israel.

5. But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?

6. But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.

7. Nevertheless, I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.

8. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment.

9. Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10. Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11. Of judgment, because the Prince of this world is judged.

12. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.

13. How be it when he, the Spirit of Truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself: but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.

14. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you. John 16/5-14.
exegesis.20: As none can fail to recognize his own son, the prophecies about and the identification of the Holy Prophet was so doubtlessly clear in the ancient scriptures, particularly in the scriptures of the Jews and the Christians and no prophet answering the given description had ever appeared anywhere in the world. The Jews and the Christians had no reasons at all, or there was not the least difficulty for them to recognize the genuine apostolic personality of the Holy Prophet.
exegesis.21:
Forging lies against God means saying or believing in things falsely relating them to God, viz. God having a son or sons and daughters or God having delegated His authority to anyone else to act on His behalf - and the similar other heathenic belief.

The tone of the set of Verses <{["Q", "6:21"]}> - <{["Q", "6:25"]}> is that of a conversation between two persons before whom the whole scene of the ultimate days was present, as going on before them. With regard to God it is obvious and with regard to the Holy Prophet will be obvious if one grasps the meaning of the actual significance of what the Holy Prophet said showing his two fingers together: '_Bo'esto ana was Sa'aa kahatain'_, i.e., I and the ultimate Hour have been sent together with the closest association towards the end of which everything is moving; which means that he is viewing every part and particle of the universe in its final position in the order of the universe as a whole (A.P.).
exegesis.23: '_Fitna'_, i.e., the lie they uttered or their disbelief would not remain any longer, but they would say 'By our Lord, ire are not polytheists.'
exegesis.25:
This and the succeeding two Verses indicate that veils were cast over their hearts because they were determined not to believe even if all the signs, i.e., miracles were shown to them. They used to visit the Holy Prophet not to listen to what he said but to dispute with him and to create doubts in the hearts of the others to obstruct the people from accepting the truth.

Abu-Sofyan, Atbah and Shaibah heard the Holy Prophet reciting the Holy Qur'an in the mosque. Nasr Ibn Khalid said '_as Muhammad recites the legends of the old, I also can relate to you the stories of the Persians._" At this, this Verse was revealed (F.A.).

In view of the significance of this passage one would restrict the significance of the clause in Verse <{["Q", "6:19"]}> to those persons that Qur'an reaches their heart. This restriction is true so far, the benefit of the guidance is concerned but as a 'Hujjat' or the argument of excuse which includes even those who hear, though it may not reach their heart and be of avail to them as explained in Verse <{["Q", "6:26"]}>. (A.P.).
exegesis.31: Feeling of sorrow or pleasure for the past actions, is one of the main features of the life here after, which is absent in the doctrine of transmigration (A.P.).
exegesis.33:
The Holy Prophet had already impressed even upon the worst of his enemies, his truthfulness, and everyone, be he his foe or a friend, had acknowledged him as '_Sadiq'_, i.e., the Truthful and '_Al-Ameen'_ - the Trustworthy. He had already earned from the people as a whole these titles even from the very beginning of his life, before his declaring his apostleship.

Hence the people's now rejecting his message, is not that they mean him a liar, but it was a denial of the bonafide of the Divine Revelation. The world around him had unanimously vouched that he had never even once been guilty of having uttered any lie or falsehood.
exegesis.34: 'There is none to change the Words of God.' The word of God means God's promises of sending the necessary help to His Apostles. It is a prophecy to say that as the apostles before the Holy Prophet were helped, he would also be surely helped.
exegesis.35:
This Verse is in reply to the extraordinary anxiety of the Holy Prophet to take all the people from the depths of ignorance, guiding them towards the truth. It is said here "_that even if you do things impossible and they get a sign; they will never be guided._"

The concluding words though addressed to the Holy Prophet not to aspire for the guidance for the ignorant ones or covet for things impossible for the arrogant ones among the people who were bent upon never to believe, are applicable to the people also.
exegesis.36:
Only those who listen, sincerely interested in knowing the truth, will believe. As for those who do not listen, they are like the dead and God will surely raise the dead on the Day of Resurrection. Then they will believe but it will be of no avail to them.

Refers to the actual purpose of the apostolic preaching in spite of its being universal but the object is the guidance of those who have aptitude for development and progress. The sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq said to his disciples '_Increase not your number by calling all sorts of people into your fold irrespective of their mental aptitude. Certainly, God has addressed those who are endowed with intellect and the power of reasoning_,' and then quoted the Verses <{["Q", "39:17"]}> and <{["Q", "39:18"]}> (A.P.).
exegesis.38:
Even the animals that walk on earth as well as those who fly, i.e., the birds, will be brought to account for the duties entrusted to them according to the native endowments, they are provided with.

'_Kitab'_ here means the Book called '_Lawh al-Mahfooz_, i.e., the Divinely Secured Tablet.

Most of the commentators are of opinion that the word 'Book' stands for the Holy Qur'an, for what the people need are the details about the religion, Islam, and in Qur'an, has been mentioned everything about the religion and the knowledge of everything has been given to the Holy Prophet and the people have been commanded to receive what he gives and to abstain from what he forbids<{["F", 1]}>; and the Qur'an has been declared to contain everything in it<{["F", 2]}>. So that the Holy Prophet may dispense with the details according to the personal capacity of each individual seeker after the Truth. The Holy Prophet had declared '_I am the City of Knowledge and 'Ali is its Gate._' Thus, after the Holy Prophet only 'Ali will be the authentic guide towards the details of the truth warranted by this declaration of the Holy Prophet who spoke nothing but the revelation from God<{["F", 3]}>.
exegesis.41:
This Verse gives out an inherent characteristic in every human being, be he a believer in God or an unbeliever, a Unitarian or a polytheist, that in the state of a total helplessness while in distress, when one finds none to help him, the inner self in him, is liberated from the restrictions of the individual's personal views, and commands him to call upon the ever-present Omnipotent One and the liberated mind automatically calls Him for the rescue.

Once a man asked the Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq, to show God to him. The Holy Imam heard him and smiled and said: '_Meet me later_.' Once the man found the Holy Imam standing alone with his companions by the side of a river. The man approached the Holy Imam with the same request. The Holy Imam commanded his companions to bind both the hands as well as the legs of the man and throw him in the river. The command of the Holy Imam was immediately carried out.
